# build-section-index.py is repo-only (no vault copy; the vault holds its OUTPUT in Automation/section-index.tsv)
# lib/registry.py and tools/registry-audit.py are repo-only (2026-07-27). PLACEMENT TEST:
#   registry.py is the sanctioned WRITE api for lead-registry.xlsx and registry-audit.py is its
#   checker. Both are invoked by local Claude Code sessions (run.sh registry-audit, check.sh);
#   Dell's side and the cloud sessions never write the registry directly, so a vault copy would
#   be a second unguarded path to the exact file this is meant to protect. Repo only, on purpose.
# tools/retrieve.py is repo-only (reads the derived index; sessions call it via run.sh retrieve)
# tools/ledger-repair.py is repo-only (2026-07-31). PLACEMENT TEST: it touches schema_migrations,
#   which only the migration runner beside it may write, and it is a ONE-TIME repair for the
#   0013-0016 ledger gap. A vault copy would put a database-mutating script on Dell's side for a
#   job his sessions must never run. Repo only, and it goes inert once the four rows exist.
# pipelines/parse_party_links.py is repo-only (2026-07-31, ORDER 17 / amendment 4). PLACEMENT
#   TEST: it is a ONE-TIME backfill that writes party_link and event rows as the DB writer, the
#   same class as pipelines/import_wave1.py and tools/ledger-repair.py. Ongoing links go through
#   the link-parties verb, so a vault copy would put a database-mutating script on Dell's side
#   for a job neither partner's sessions should ever run twice. Repo only, on purpose.
# pipelines/cadence_engine.py, pipelines/availability_matcher.py and
#   pipelines/cadence-rules-seed.sql are repo-only (2026-07-31, ORDER 14). PLACEMENT TEST:
#   both scripts are steps of bin/nightly.sh, which is itself repo-only and runs on Joe's Mac
#   under Joe's credentials; the engine WRITES next_action + event rows as the DB writer, and
#   the seed file writes cadence_rule. A vault copy would put database-mutating jobs on Dell's
#   side that his sessions must never run — and when Dell's nightly lands it authors its own,
#   the same reference-pattern ruling ops/scheduled-tasks got after ORDER 8. What Dell DOES see
#   is the OUTPUT: the actions the engine spawns land in the exported files he already reads.
# pipelines/review_queue.py, pipelines/brief_pack.py and
#   pipelines/notification-budget-seed.sql are repo-only (2026-07-31, ORDER 16). PLACEMENT TEST:
#   both scripts read the database through Joe's exporter credential and read HIS calendar,
#   HIS open items, and HIS documents, so a vault copy would be a second runtime pointed at
#   one partner's data, which is the opposite of what a shared file is for. They are invoked
#   through run.sh by the heartbeat and the Monday brief, exactly like health-check.py. Dell's
#   twin gets its own pair when his side lands, computing from HIS credential, the same
#   reference-pattern ruling ORDER 14 took. The seed file writes system_config, so it carries
#   the same never-on-Dell's-side reason as the cadence seed above.
# tools/writing-lint.py is repo-only FOR NOW (2026-07-25). It enforces a SHARED-tier doctrine
#   file (DNA/writing-rules.md), so Dell's side would benefit from a vault copy — but adding a
#   file to the shared tier is a two-writer decision for Joe, not a unilateral write. Placement
#   test: repo, because it is a checker like health-check.py/retrieve.py that local sessions
#   invoke via run.sh, and its fixtures + baseline need version history to mean anything.
#   Promote to shared/ -> DNA/ when Joe says so. Fixtures + baseline live with it.
